title: Little words: a, de, en, con, para, desde, hasta
topic: simple prepositions and how they're used
why: The first lesson of the “around town” unit sorts out the simple prepositions (a, de, en, con, para, desde, hasta, entre), starting from the mix-ups English speakers typically make. It builds on al and del and the verbs of movement from the previous unit, and gets you ready for hay / está and asking for directions.

{"lessons": ["

A, de, en: the three pillars

Prepositions are short but sneaky: they never map neatly onto English. Start with the three most common ones.

PrepositionUseExample
adirection, destination (to)Voy a Madrid. / Voy al médico.
aclock time (at)La clase empieza a las diez.
apersonal a (no English equivalent)Espero a Lucía.
deorigin (from)Soy de Lyon. / Vengo del trabajo.
depossession (’s, of)el coche de Pablo
dematerial, contentsuna mesa de madera, un vaso de agua
enplace, no movement (in, at)Vivo en Sevilla. / Estoy en casa.
enin, onLas llaves están en la mesa.
enmeans of transportation (by)Voy en tren. (but a pie, on foot)
enmonth, season, year (in)en mayo, en verano

Trap #1: at, in, on

Good news first: for cities, English already does what Spanish does. “To” for movement, “in” for being there:

EnglishSpanish
I'm going to Madrid.Voy a Madrid. (movement)
I'm in Madrid.Estoy en Madrid. (no movement)
I live in Madrid.Vivo en Madrid.

The real trap is that English has three words for location, “at,” “in” and “on,” and Spanish uses just one for all of them: at home, in the kitchen, on the table, at the station all take the same little word. Don't go looking for a separate “on” or “at.”

The question to ask yourself: is there movement toward the place? Yes: a. No: en.

Vivo en Valencia, pero mañana voy a Madrid en tren.I live in Valencia, but tomorrow I'm going to Madrid by train.
", "

Con, para, desde, hasta, entre

PrepositionUseExample
conwithCeno con Marta. / un café con leche
parapurpose: (in order) to + verbEstudio español para trabajar en Madrid.
pararecipient: forEste regalo es para Lucía.
desde… hastafrom… to, from… until (time, place)desde las nueve hasta las dos / desde Madrid hasta Toledo
de… afrom… to (shorter)Trabajo de nueve a cinco.
entrebetween, amongEl banco está entre la farmacia y el bar.

Conmigo, contigo

After a preposition, “me” is mí (with an accent) and “you” is ti (no accent): para mí, para ti. But with con, they fuse into a single word:

With…Spanish
meconmigo
you (tú)contigo
him, her, you (usted)con él, con ella, con usted
uscon nosotros, con nosotras
you (plural)con vosotros, con vosotras
themcon ellos, con ellas

Exception: after entre, you keep yo and tú: entre tú y yo (between you and me).

In this lesson, English “for” is para. Spanish has a second word, por, which you'll study later; for now, para is all you need for purpose and recipient.

¿Vienes conmigo? Sí, voy contigo.Are you coming with me? Yes, I'm going with you.
", "

Traps for English speakers

Here are the mistakes English speakers make most often. Read each line, comparing the two columns.

EnglishSpanishWhy
on the trainen el tren“on” and “in” = en
at Marta's (I'm having dinner)en casa de Martano “’s”: say “in the house of”
to Marta's (I'm going)a casa de Martamovement: a
my mother's housela casa de mi madreno “’s”: possession with de, the owner comes last
the eight o'clock trainel tren de las ochothe time keeps its article and comes after
in Mayen mayosame as English
on Monday (this Monday)el lunesno preposition before a day: no “on”
a wooden tableuna mesa de maderamaterial goes after, with de

Mi (my) comes up in the next unit; for now, just remember the pattern la casa de…

Don't forget al and del

They come back with all these prepositions: Voy al centro, Vuelvo del trabajo, el coche del profesor, desde el parque hasta el río (no contraction with desde or with en: only with a and de).

Esta noche ceno en casa de Carmen y después voy al cine con ella.Tonight I'm having dinner at Carmen's, and afterwards I'm going to the movies with her.
